llm.summary: This is a documentation-only orchestration skill for MCP-heavy workflows, with no executable payload, but it can influence agents to use MCP tools and subagents more broadly than some users may expect.

dimensions.detail: The artifacts consistently describe routing large, multi-step data or tool-chain workflows through MCP patterns, validation, and subagent coordination; these capabilities fit the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The body text includes broad automatic-use keywords such as code execution, MCP, pattern, optimize, check, monitor, and break down, but the installed frontmatter trigger is narrower and the skill also states when not to use it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains only Markdown skill files and metadata; it states there is no separate install step or CLI entry point, and static scan and VirusTotal telemetry are clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is proportionate for data-heavy MCP workflows, but users should understand it may route work through available MCP connectors and subagents in the current Claude Code environment.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Examples mention external state, intermediate-result storage, and debug logging, but no actual storage backend, persistence mechanism, credential access, or background worker is included in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install this if you want an agent to optimize large MCP/tool-chain workflows. Review your available MCP connectors and subagent permissions first, because this skill may encourage routing workflow data through those tools and may pause or restructure work when its validation guidance detects context-risk conditions.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The scanner's broad-trigger concern is supported by body text in the hub and modules, but the behavior is disclosed, related to MCP workflow routing, and partly narrowed by explicit workflow-size and complexity guidance.
[SQP-2] expected: The validation module's ability to inspect workflow data and stop or decompose execution is disclosed and purpose-aligned for MECW compliance, though users should be aware it can interrupt workflows.
